sum: Jefferies has reiterated its hold rating on LVMH with a price target of 415 euros, even as analyst James Grzinic trimmed his 2027 estimates below consensus on the back of persistently unfavourable demand conditions. The endorsement of the valuation came without any softening in his view of the trading environment, which he still describes as difficult.

The stock had strung together four consecutive sessions of gains through Thursday, a run media reports chalked up to a short-term recovery in the luxury sector and broader industry sentiment rather than any fresh company-specific catalyst. That streak snapped on Friday, when the shares gave up 0.6%.

Attention is also turning to the French capital's pavements. According to Le Monde, Louis Vuitton has committed up to 2 million euros to redesign two Paris streets adjacent to its forthcoming flagship store on the Champs-Élysées. The arrangement, reported on Tuesday, has stirred debate over the private financing of public spaces and the sway that private backers can exert over how those spaces are shaped.

On the legal front, the investigating magistrate overseeing the French inquiry into Hermès shares was planning to summon Bernard Arnault, Le Monde reported on 30 October. Jean-Jacques Guiony, a member of LVMH's executive committee, has already been questioned — explicitly in the capacity of a witness. For Arnault, the newspaper reported only the judge's intention to call him, not any questioning that has taken place. LVMH declined to comment on the ongoing proceedings.

The shares were down 1.4% today, a decline media coverage attributed to a broad selloff on the Paris bourse led by retreating US technology stocks, with other luxury names also coming under pressure. No company-specific trigger for that move was identified.

Louis Vuitton, meanwhile, has confirmed the appointment of Hector Muelas to lead creative brand direction, a decision ratified on 23 October and effective from 1 November. In the newly created role of Chief Brand Creative Officer, he reports to deputy chief executive Damien Bertrand and takes charge of brand storytelling and campaigns.

LVMH Discloses 494.6 Million Shares as Zenith Weighs Swiss Job Cuts
sum: LVMH has laid out its capital structure as of 31 October, reporting 494,606,080 outstanding shares in a regulatory disclosure. The filing puts gross voting rights at 743,358,184 and net voting rights at 739,382,278 — three separate figures that describe different facets of the group's ownership base. The notice is a snapshot at a fixed date, not a signal of any new transaction.

That distinction matters, because the disclosure lands alongside two unrelated developments at the French luxury giant: a repositioning at its watch brand Zenith and a French judicial review of the group's historical Hermès stake.

Zenith confirmed on 23 October that it will pivot toward higher-end timepieces and lower production volumes. The LVMH-owned brand simultaneously opened an employee consultation on the plan. According to media reports, as many as half of its Swiss workforce could be affected by job cuts.

No final decision on redundancies is expected before the consultation closes on 12 November, meaning the potential staff reductions remain undecided. The strategic shift itself, by contrast, has already been confirmed by the brand.

French investigators are also examining LVMH's role in the acquisition of Hermès shares. As Le Monde reported on 30 October, the probe into the vanished shares of Hermès heir Nicolas Puech has shifted its focus to that question. The investigating magistrate reportedly plans to summon Bernard Arnault — a reported procedural step in an ongoing inquiry, not a finding of wrongdoing.

The judge has also questioned LVMH executive Jean-Jacques Guiony about the historical purchase of a 17% stake in Hermès, linked to Puech's missing shares. LVMH has said it will not comment on pending proceedings. The scrutiny concerns the group's past stake-building in a rival, not its own shares covered by today's disclosure — and the filing offers no answer to those legal questions.

LVMH shares slipped 1.2% yesterday. On the corporate calendar, the Zenith consultation wraps up on 12 November, and the group's Nona Source platform — which reuses luxury materials — holds a sale in Paris from 24 to 28 November, a part of the business distinct from the watch brand's overhaul.

sum: LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton reported mixed nine-month results for the period ended September 30, 2026, with group growth masking a deeper setback in its largest business. World Footwear reported the figures on November 4, citing the company statement and comments from Chief Financial Officer Cécile Cabanis.
LVMH stock real-time quote traded at 406.40 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 12:16 CET on Wednesday, November 4, 2026.

Revenue reached 57.1 billion euros in the first nine months, down 2% on a reported basis but up 2% organically from the same period a year earlier. Organic growth strips out currency and portfolio effects, making it the clearer indicator of underlying trading momentum in the company report.

Third-quarter organic revenue increased 1% year on year to 18.5 billion euros. The result showed that LVMH continued to benefit from the breadth of its portfolio, but regional trends diverged. Business activity remained positive in the United States, Europe and Japan, while China became more subdued.

Fashion and Leather Goods, the group's largest division, generated 26.4 billion euros in the first nine months. Reported revenue declined 4% and organic revenue fell 2% from the comparable period in 2025. The deterioration accelerated in the third quarter, when divisional revenue fell 5% after a 1% increase in the second quarter.

Cabanis said the quarter brought a more challenging Chinese consumer backdrop, with consumer sentiment deteriorating at the beginning of the period. She also identified the Middle East situation as an additional headwind. The comments point to a demand problem concentrated in an important market rather than a broad contraction across every LVMH business.

All other LVMH divisions reported growth in the third quarter, according to the report. That diversification offers some protection for group revenue, but Fashion and Leather Goods remains central to the investment case because Louis Vuitton and Dior give the division disproportionate influence over the group's growth profile and investor sentiment.

sum: Genpact Limited, an agentic and advanced technology solutions company, provides digital transformation, business process management, technology, data, analytics, and artificial intelligence (AI) services to enterprises in India, the rest of Asia, North and Latin America, and Europe. Its Financial Services segment offers customer onboarding, customer service, collections, retail and commercial loan operations, payment operations, mortgage origination and servicing, compliance, wealth management, capital market operations support, financial crime and risk management, proprietary insurance policy suite, underwriting support, new business processing, policy administration, customer, claims management, catastrophe and exposure/risk modeling, actuarial services, end-to-end third-party administration for property and casualty claims, and technology services. The company's Consumer and Healthcare segment provides demand generation, sensing and planning, supply chain planning and management, pricing and trade promotion management, deduction recovery management, order management, digital commerce, customer experience, lifecycle management, regulatory operations, chemistry manufacturing control compliance, regulatory information management, claims processing and adjudication, claims recovery and payment integrity, revenue cycle management, health equity analytics, and care services. Its High Tech and Manufacturing segment offers solutions for trust and safety, advertising sales support, customer and user experience, customer care support, supply chain management, direct and indirect procurement, logistics, field, aftermarket support, and engineering services. It offers digital operations, data-tech-AI, advisory, agent technology; and finance and accounting, human resources, sales and commercial operations, marketing, and global business solutions. The company has strategic alliance with Google Cloud. The company was founded in 1997 and is based in Hamilton, Bermuda.

"He's down 50%": Sam Altman's stock tips to buy Hermès, LVMH, shock Nikhil Kamath as luxury giants take a hit
sum: Zerodha co-founder Nikhil Kamath has recalled an interesting exchange with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, revealing that the artificial intelligence pioneer had recommended luxury stocks Hermès and LVMH when asked which companies investors should consider buying.

However, the picks have reportedly lost around 50% of their value since then, prompting Kamath to question whether the productivity gains promised by artificial intelligence are translating into real economic benefits.
Kamath shared the anecdote during a recent episode of his podcast, WTF is AI?, where he was joined by a panel of technology experts to discuss the AI boom.
The conversation has since attracted attention on social media, with users debating Altman's investment thesis and the gap between expectations surrounding AI and the economic reality.
The exchange originally took place when Kamath interviewed Altman last year. Recalling the conversation, Kamath said he had asked the OpenAI chief which stocks he should buy.
According to Kamath's recollection, Altman's recommendation was based on the expectation that artificial intelligence would dramatically improve productivity.
The underlying argument was that as AI tools make individuals and businesses more productive, people would eventually have greater financial resources and disposable income.

items.t: LVMH Denies Puech Hermès Stake Interest as Zenith Weighs Swiss Cuts
sum: LVMH has flatly rejected a report that it wants to buy Nicolas Puech's stake in Hermès, pushing back on a Le Monde story published Friday that surfaced amid a judicial probe into shares belonging to the Hermès heir that have reportedly gone missing. The denial lands alongside a separate, unrelated disclosure: the luxury group's own share buybacks, detailed in a regulatory notice Tuesday covering repurchases made between October 19 and 23, with the stated purpose of cancelling the stock under a program approved on April 23.

The two threads — a criminal investigation touching LVMH's history with Hermès stock and a routine capital measure involving LVMH's own equity — concern entirely different matters and should not be conflated, the company's filings imply.

At the center of the Le Monde account is Jean-Jacques Guiony, an LVMH executive questioned as a voluntary witness by an investigating magistrate about the group's historical purchases of Hermès shares. The probe itself focuses on stock that Puech's former wealth manager is alleged to have sold. LVMH has denied any intention of taking over Puech's holding.

For investors, the gap between what is being investigated and what has actually been established matters. The report describes a witness interview and the company's position — nothing more. It does not demonstrate any unlawful acquisition by LVMH, nor does it assign the group responsibility for the missing shares. The rejection of takeover intent is likewise the company's own statement, not a court finding.

Away from the legal headlines, LVMH is reshaping its brands. At Louis Vuitton, Hector Muelas steps into the newly created role of Chief Brand Creative Officer today, taking charge of creative brand communications and campaigns and reporting to deputy CEO Damien Bertrand, according to media reports. The appointment was announced on October 23. It gives the brand's creative presentation its own leadership post — a decision about marketing and campaigns, not a signal of recovering demand or rising sales.
Zenith, the group's watchmaker, is charting a different course.

Bernard Arnault's business-first strategy with foreign heads of state, from Trump to Putin
sum: Buffets were set up all around the grounds of this magnificent 19th-century hôtel particulier, which serves as the residence for American ambassadors in France, just a few steps from the Elysée Palace. Was it that rather kitsch orchestra accompanying "O Sole Mio" and other popular Italian songs sung by Andrea Bocelli, wearing a jacket and blue-tinted aviator glasses, in front of 2,000 guests in cocktail attire? Or perhaps, a little further away and protected by security officers, that small circle of leading industry executives and VIP guests greeting Charles Kushner, father of Jared Kushner – the son-in-law and business associate of Donald Trump? It felt like a scene straight out of the opening of Francis Ford Coppola's The Godfather (1972).

Thousands of kilometers away, in Washington, on the eve of July 4, the US president was preparing to kick off the celebrations for the 250th anniversary of US independence. Meanwhile, in Paris, "the honorable Charles Kushner" – pardoned by Trump after being convicted of financial misconduct and subsequently appointed by him as ambassador to Paris – decided to mark the occasion by paying tribute to a Frenchman whose "commercial success is legendary": Bernard Arnault, the "guest of honor," whose name was printed in gold letters on the invitations.

One hour before most of the guests flooded into the embassy's sprawling gardens, a private party of the roughly 80 most generous guests had already gathered around Kushner and the LVMH chief executive. Alongside Arnault, accompanied by three of his sons – Antoine, Alexandre and Frédéric – were Patrick Pouyanné, the CEO of TotalEnergies, Alexandre Ricard, CEO of Pernod Ricard, and Slawomir Krupa and Jean-Laurent Bonnafé, the heads of Société Générale and BNP Paribas banks. All had contributed their share – at least €100,000 each, with the Arnault family contributing €3 million of the €9 million raised by the embassy – to fund the celebrations as well as the renovation of the splendid three-story building.
